target.title: fix(codex): prevent corrupted emoji in sandbox HTTP failures
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server tools using sandbox `http/request` could receive a corrupted failure message when a long helper stderr diagnostic placed an emoji at the retained-tail boundary. The surfaced JSON-RPC error began with a replacement character instead of a complete Unicode character.

## Why This Change Was Made

The streaming sandbox HTTP stderr owner now decodes UTF-8 continuously across pipe chunks, then uses the repository's surrogate-safe negative slice helper when retaining its existing 4096-code-unit tail. This preserves the current size limit, child lifecycle, JSON-RPC/body-delta behavior, and non-streaming request path; no schema, protocol, configuration, or sandbox policy changes are included.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox HTTP failures keep readable emoji and other supplementary Unicode characters at the stderr tail boundary instead of displaying `�` in the tool error.

## Evidence

- Red regressions: the retained-tail case began with isolated low surrogate `0xde00`; a separate real-child case split the emoji's UTF-8 bytes across delayed stderr writes and surfaced `A���B` instead of `A😀B`.
- Current-head runtime proof uses the production `httpRequest -> runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest -> readStreamingSandboxHttpResponse` path with a real child process that splits the emoji bytes across stderr writes and also places it at the retained-tail boundary:

  ```text
  {"path":"httpRequest -> real child split UTF-8 stderr -> readStreamingSandboxHttpResponse -> Error","messageLength":4095,"firstCodeUnit":"42","unpairedSurrogate":false,"exactExpectedTail":true,"utf8RoundTripStartsWithReplacement":false}
  ```

- Focused owner test file:

  ```text
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  9 passed (9)
  ```

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passed for both changed files.
- Targeted `oxlint` passed for both changed files.

target.title: test(sessions): seed SQLite transcript freshness
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Current main CI deterministically fails three terminal-session integration surfaces after transcript freshness moved from JSONL file mtimes to SQLite mutation watermarks. The command, gateway, and auto-reply fixtures still touched legacy JSONL files, so they no longer created the transcript state the production reader checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Seed real-store transcript activity through `appendTranscriptEvent`, the same storage-neutral session accessor used by runtime code and lifecycle tests. Model registry observation by ordering the transcript append before or after the registry write, and model the gateway owner boundary with explicit mutation/observed watermarks. Keep legacy-looking `sessionFile` values so reset/resume assertions still cover those fields without treating them as freshness sources.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. Main CI now tests the SQLite-backed terminal-session contract instead of an obsolete filesystem implementation detail.

## Evidence

- Exact main failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29177284308/job/86608682983
- Blacksmith Testbox: three consecutive runs across command, gateway, auto-reply, and lifecycle suites — 1,869/1,869 assertions passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox final focused rerun after type hardening — 623/623 assertions passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox changed-surface gate — passed.
- Fresh autoreview — no actionable findings.

No agent transcript attached, per maintainer instruction.
